memos.headline: Momentum leaders S10, S04, S06 stretched to overbought; S02 and S08 remain broken downtrends
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe as of June 27. The strongest relative-strength names—S10 (+43% over 12w, at its 52w high, RSI 76.6), S04 (+30% over 12w, RSI 77, just 0.3% off highs), and S06 (+18% over 12w, RSI 75.6)—are all trading 10–22% above their 50-day means, which historically flags near-term mean-reversion risk even if the intermediate trend is clearly up. On the other side, S02 is in a catastrophic downtrend: -51% from its 52w high, 38% below its 200-day mean, and 12w relative strength vs SPY of -50.5%, making it untouchable until it can reclaim its 50-day average. S08 is similarly weak at -22% from highs and -10% below its 200d mean, though its RSI near 50 suggests the selling has at least paused. I favor S03 and S07 as the best risk/reward longs—both show strong 4w momentum (+8.6% and +9.4%) with RSIs in the mid-to-upper 60s/70s and improving relative strength, but are not as extended as S10 or S04.

views.note: At 52w high with RSI 76.6 and 22% above 50d mean—trend is powerful but too extended for fresh entry; would buy a pullback to ~140 (near 50d mean).
RSI 77 and 11% above 50d mean near all-time highs; trend is undeniable but risk/reward poor for new longs—a close below 470 would concern me.
Strong 4w +8.6% move with RSI 67.9 not yet overbought, 11% above 50d mean but still 8% off highs—would stop below 200 (near 200d mean).
Best 4w return in universe at +9.4% with improving relative strength (+5.1% vs SPY), RSI 75 is elevated but 7.7% off highs leaves room; stop below 360.
Near 52w highs with +20.5% 26w return and strong relative strength, but RSI 75.6 and 10% above 50d mean warrant tight stops below 270.
Down 51% from highs, 38% below 200d mean, 12w relative strength vs SPY -50.5%—this is a broken chart; would reconsider only above 350 (near 50d mean).
Persistent downtrend: -22% from highs, 10% below 200d mean, negative relative strength on all timeframes; need a close above 210 to reconsider.
Weak relative strength (-9.4% vs SPY over 4w), below both moving averages, RSI 44—no reason to own until price reclaims 165 area.
RSI 61 and 7.7% above 50d mean look constructive, but flat 4w relative strength vs SPY and -13.5% drawdown from highs leave me unconvinced; watching 170 as support.
RSI 52.6 and near its 50d mean suggest consolidation; -4.6% last week is a red flag—need to hold 105 or risk resuming the 12w -8% downtrend.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Lead on Margin Expansion; S07 and S09 Show Earnings Compression That Warrants Caution
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in S10 (42.6% net margin, +69.2% YoY revenue, minimal debt at $8.5B) and S05 (38.3% net margin, +46% YoY net income growth on 12% revenue growth with only $14.8B debt). S04 also stands out with 36.9% net margin and +17.7% net income growth on solid 13.3% revenue growth. On the other end, S07 is contracting sharply—revenue down 9.8% YoY and net income down 29.8%—while carrying $31.7B in debt against just $14.3B in quarterly revenue, which signals real cash-flow risk. S09 is essentially flat on revenue (+0.1%) with net income declining 6.2% and a thin 9.3% margin, leaving little cushion. I would need to see a reversal in S07's top-line trajectory and S09's margin trend before getting constructive on either name.

views.note: 69% YoY revenue growth, 42.6% net margin, and only $8.5B total debt make this the strongest fundamental profile in the universe.
38.3% net margin with +46% net income growth and a clean balance sheet ($14.8B debt) signals durable, expanding earnings power.
13.3% revenue growth translating into 17.7% net income growth at a 36.9% margin with manageable $42.9B debt is high-quality compounding.
Revenue +8.6% and net income +64.2% look impressive, but the 11% net margin suggests the earnings jump may reflect one-time items rather than structural improvement—need to see margin durability.
Solid 26% margin but only +5.1% revenue growth and $92.2B in total debt; earnings power is stable but not accelerating.
32.3% net margin is attractive but $407B total debt dwarfs quarterly revenue; leverage trajectory is the key variable to watch.
Flat revenue (+0.1%) and declining net income (-6.2%) at a thin 9.3% margin with $32.8B debt signals cash-flow compression risk.
Revenue contracting 9.8% and net income down 29.8% with $31.7B debt against $14.3B quarterly revenue is a deteriorating earnings profile I refuse to pay for.
Revenue +9.8% is decent but 5.7% net margin is the thinnest in the universe and net income YoY is unavailable, making earnings durability hard to assess.
19.1% margin is respectable but revenue is declining 2.1% YoY and net income is essentially flat (+0.4%); need top-line stabilization before turning constructive.

memos.headline: Fed on Extended Pause at 4.50% With Softening Labor Market and Benign Inflation — Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth, Lean Into Banks on Steepening Curve
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has sat at 4.50% for three months with no change, while CPI is running at just 2.4% y/y and unemployment has drifted up 40bp over the past year to 4.3%. The 10y-2y spread has steepened sharply (+95bp over 12 months to +0.56pp), which is a classic pre-easing signal and a tailwind for bank net interest margins. The 10y yield at 4.29% is flat year-over-year and down 9bp over three months, suggesting the long end is already pricing in a growth slowdown without a panic. My base case is that the next move is a cut — likely in H2 2025 — which favors duration-sensitive growth and banks while making cyclicals and energy more vulnerable. A CPI print re-accelerating above 3% y/y or unemployment dropping back below 4.0% would force me to revisit this easing-bias call.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits most from a pause-to-easing transition with 10y yields drifting lower and inflation contained at 2.4% y/y.
Banks should benefit from the steepening curve (+56bp 10y-2y spread, up 95bp y/y) which supports NIM expansion even before actual rate cuts arrive.
Staples offer defensive positioning but limited upside in a regime where the labor market is softening only gradually and no recession is imminent.
Cyclicals face headwinds from rising unemployment (+0.4pp y/y) and a slowing economy, but the pause regime limits downside for now.
Energy tends to underperform in late-cycle slowdowns; rising unemployment and an easing-biased Fed suggest demand headwinds ahead.
Rate-sensitive sectors gain as the 10y yield edges lower and the market prices in eventual easing from the current 4.50% hold.

memos.headline: Limited Sentiment Differentiation Across Universe; S10 Earnings Reaction and S02 Leadership Churn Stand Out
memos.body: I have very little GDELT-style media tone data to work with this cycle—my evidence set is almost entirely 8-K filings rather than media coverage volume or tone scores. That said, I can extract directional signals from the nature and cadence of disclosures. S10 is the clearest positive: its May 28 earnings 8-K triggered a +3.2% one-day price reaction, suggesting the results surprised to the upside and narrative may still be turning. S02 is the most active filer with four 8-Ks in six weeks, three involving officer departures/appointments, which typically generates negative or uncertain media tone and signals organizational instability. S01 had a Deutsche Bank presentation and a named officer announcement (Arnold) in early June, which could be narrative-positive if the market reads it as strategic refresh, but the signal is ambiguous. S09's earnings reaction was a muted +0.4%, suggesting the result was already priced and media tone likely flat.

views.note: Earnings 8-K drove +3.2% price pop on May 28-29, suggesting positive narrative shift that may not yet be fully reflected.
Three officer departure/appointment filings in six weeks signals leadership churn likely generating negative or uncertain media tone.
Deutsche Bank presentation and officer announcement could shift narrative either way; insufficient tone data to take a directional view.
Earnings reaction of only +0.4% suggests results were in-line and media tone is likely flat—no edge here.
Two routine filings (Other Events and shareholder vote) with no price reaction data; no discernible sentiment shift.
Reg FD disclosure and shareholder vote are standard seasonal filings with no tone signal.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Declining Sharply but Still Elevated; Geopolitical Tail Risk Receding for Now
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has fallen 24% over three months to 239.86, and the VIX has dropped nearly 20% in a month to 16.59, signaling that the acute phase of policy-driven volatility (tariffs, export controls, sanctions rhetoric) is fading. HY spreads at 3.04% confirm credit markets are not pricing imminent disruption. WTI at $66.44 is down 5.2% over three months despite a recent monthly bounce, suggesting energy supply-chain stress is contained and OPEC+ discipline is loosening—this is a mild headwind for energy-exposed names but a tailwind for cost-sensitive industrials and consumers. I lack granular GDELT event data on specific sanctions or export-control escalations, so my conviction is moderate; a renewed tariff round or China semiconductor ban would force me to revisit. The 8-K filings across the universe are routine Reg FD and Other Events disclosures with no red flags pointing to sanctions exposure or supply-chain disruption.

views.note: Two Reg FD filings in early June suggest active investor communication but no geopolitical catalyst visible; staying neutral until content is clearer.
Recent 8.01 filing on June 20 and earlier Reg FD disclosure are routine; declining policy uncertainty is mildly supportive but no structural edge.
Falling policy uncertainty and contained energy costs reduce geopolitical headwinds; 8.01 filing in May was uneventful, and the macro backdrop is improving.
Active disclosure cadence (two 8-Ks in a month) amid declining VIX and policy uncertainty suggests management is positioning proactively; no sanctions or export-control risk flagged.
Single early-May Reg FD filing and no subsequent updates leave me with insufficient geopolitical signal; would need clarity on supply-chain or China exposure to take a view.
Reg FD disclosure in mid-May is stale; declining HY spreads are supportive but I have no evidence of specific geopolitical tailwind or risk.
